answer_text:
Here is a comprehensive **7-Day China Trip Itinerary** — following the classic "Golden Triangle" route of **Beijing → Xi'an → Chengdu → Shanghai**, perfect for first-time visitors who want history, culture, nature, and city life all in one week!

---

# 🇨🇳 7-Day China Trip Itinerary

This itinerary takes you from the historic charm of Beijing and Xi'an, to the pandas in Chengdu, and the bright city lights of Shanghai — a nice mix of history, food, architecture, and local experiences, perfect for first-time visitors who want a bit of everything.

---

## 📅 Day 1 — Arrival in Beijing
**Welcome to the Capital!**

Welcome to Beijing! Once you land, you're right in the middle of China's rich history. Start your day with a walk through Tiananmen Square, one of the biggest public squares in the world.

- 🏨 **Stay:** A hotel in the Dongcheng district gives great access to major attractions.
- 🌆 **Evening:** Spend your evening walking through the vibrant Dongcheng district.
- 💡 **Tip:** Get WeChat and a VPN before you arrive since most Western apps don't work in China.

---

## 📅 Day 2 — Beijing: Forbidden City & Hutongs

Visit the most iconic sights in and around the capital city, including the 15th-century Temple of Heaven, the Forbidden City, and the historic Tiananmen Square.

- 🏛️ **Morning:** Start your day at Tiananmen Square around 7:30 AM before the crowds arrive. Head to Jingshan Park for excellent views of the Forbidden City.
- 🏘️ **Afternoon:** Explore the traditional hutongs around Nanluoguxiang.
- 👟 **Tip:** Wear good walking shoes — you'll walk 5–6 miles on uneven ground.

---

## 📅 Day 3 — Beijing: The Great Wall

- 🧱 **Morning:** Visit the Mutianyu section of the Great Wall. It's less busy than Badaling and the views are better. Take the early bus to get more time at the wall.
- 🌙 **Evening:** At night, take the overnight train to Xi'an. Beijing and Xi'an are just 4.5 hours apart by train — a perfect mix of history and modernity.

---

## 📅 Day 4 — Xi'an: Terracotta Warriors

- 🗿 **Morning:** Start your day with a visit to the world-famous Terracotta Warriors, thousands of life-sized clay soldiers that have been standing guard for over 2,000 years. It's a truly impressive sight and one of China's greatest historical treasures.
- 🕌 **Afternoon:** Visit the historic Giant Wild Goose Pagoda. An optional evening trip to Great Tang All Day Mall offers lively performances and Tang-style architecture.
- 🚲 **Day 5 Preview:** Ride a bike along the ancient Xi'an City Wall, one of the best-preserved city walls in China.

---

## 📅 Day 5 — Xi'an to Chengdu: Giant Pandas 🐼

- ✈️ **Travel:** Head to Chengdu by flight or high-speed train, depending on what suits your schedule.
- 🏮 **Arrival:** Slow things down with a walk along Jinli Ancient Street. This charming area is full of glowing lanterns, traditional architecture, and delicious Sichuan snacks. It's the perfect place to get a feel for Chengdu's laid-back vibe.
- 🐼 **Day 6 Preview:** Get to the Giant Panda Breeding Center when it opens at 7:30 AM to see the pandas eat breakfast.

---

## 📅 Day 6 — Chengdu: Pandas, Parks & Local Life

- 🐼 **Morning:** No trip to China is complete without visiting the pandas. Watch these adorable creatures munching bamboo in their natural habitat.
- 🌿 **Afternoon:** Relax at Renmin Park, where locals enjoy tea and mahjong, or take a stroll down Jinli Old Street for souvenirs.
- ✈️ **Evening:** Fly to Shanghai (approximately 2 hours).

---

## 📅 Day 7 — Shanghai: The Bund, Yu Garden & Farewell

- 🌇 **Morning:** Stroll along The Bund to admire the striking skyline across the river. Then explore the classical beauty of Yu Garden and its bustling surrounding market.
- 🥟 **Lunch:** Don't miss the famous Xiao Long Bao (soup dumplings) at the original Nanxiang restaurant nearby — a true Shanghai classic!
- 🛍️ **Afternoon:** Wander through Yuyuan Bazaar and sample Shanghai's famous xiaolongbao. In the afternoon, take a leisurely stroll along Nanjing Road before heading to The Bund, where colonial-era buildings blend seamlessly with futuristic skyscrapers.
- ✈️ **Departure:** Visit the Shanghai Museum to gain deeper insight into Chinese art and history before heading to the airport for departure.

---

## ✅ Essential Travel Tips

### 🛂 Visas
China currently offers visa-free entry for up to 30 days to ordinary passport holders from 47 countries, including much of Europe, Australia, New Zealand, South Korea, Japan, and several South American nations. A 7-day trip fits easily within this allowance. Visa policies update regularly, so confirm the latest requirements with your local Chinese embassy or consulate before booking.

### 📱 Tech & Apps
In China, some overseas websites are blocked. Popular sites such as Google, YouTube, Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram are not accessible. If you need to use these platforms, it is strongly recommended that you purchase and install a VPN before arriving in China.

Once you arrive in China, you will notice that almost all vendors accept mobile payments, from large shopping malls to local vendors. This means you can buy almost anything using just your phone. The most popular mobile payment options are Alipay and WeChat Pay.
